what: What an OutLayer TESTNET custody wallet can do, and what its wallet policy (Layer A) actually enforces. Probed live on 2026-11-13 with scripts/testnet/outlayer-probe.ts. Every tx below is on public NEAR testnet and its actions can be listed with: npx tsx scripts/dev/tx-inspect.ts <wallet> <txHash>. Findings are reported as observed, including the ones that go against us and one earlier reading of ours that turned out to be wrong (F3).

findings.claim: An OutLayer testnet wallet signs arbitrary contract calls (POST /wallet/v1/call): wrap NEAR, register storage, and swap on Ref Finance via ft_transfer_call.

evidence.note: 0.1 wNEAR in, 4,251,695 USDT.e out of Ref pool #57 (that pool had drifted far from market; see docs/CUSTODY.md), received in the wallet

findings.claim: A call to a contract that is not on the policy whitelist is refused by OutLayer before signing: 403 policy_denied "Address 'attacker-unlisted.testnet' is not in whitelist". A NATIVE NEAR transfer to an unlisted account, or above the per-transaction cap, is refused the same way (403 policy_denied, "Per-transaction limit exceeded for native").

evidence.note: refusals are HTTP responses, so there is no tx; the policy that produced them is stored in the tx above. The same refusals are recorded inside the full run: data/demo-run/custody-run.json

findings.claim: POST /wallet/v1/transfer with a `token` field does NOT send the token. It ignores the field, answers status success with a tx hash, and sends `amount` as yoctoNEAR: the txs below are Transfer{deposit:5000 / 2000 / 2000} actions and the wallet's USDT.e balance did not move. Our first probe read the success as a token transfer; the end-to-end run caught it (payouts reported paid, balances unchanged). Quiet Treasury therefore sends every token payout as an ft_transfer through /call.

evidence.note: the same endpoint refused an unlisted recipient with 403 because it was a NATIVE transfer to an unlisted account (F2), not because it inspected a token

findings.claim: An ft_transfer sent through POST /wallet/v1/call is not inspected: the recipient inside the call arguments is not checked, only the outer contract. A transfer to an account that is not on the whitelist succeeded.
findings.consequence: Layer A bounds which contracts the wallet may touch and how much native NEAR may move, but it cannot restrict who receives a token payout. Payout recipients are enforced by Layer B (executor guards + the DAO-approved terms).

findings.claim: A per-token amount limit was not enforced for a token sent through /call: with limits.per_transaction[usdt.fakes.testnet] = 1000, an ft_transfer of 5000 went through.
findings.consequence: Token amounts are bounded by Layer B (price floor, chunk sizes, the budget on the mandate contract). Daily token limits were not retested after F3 (the first daily probe used the native-dust path and proves nothing). Mainnet semantics were not tested.
